# `Demonstrate`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Function-state notification of the demonstration mount loop.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER (observation only) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ (emitter, payload members and stop cancel); INFERRED (event name; skip-end option unset) |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, StartDemonstrate @0x17d1f0, DemonstrateFunc @0x1866e0, StopDemonstrate @0x17d350, FUNC_STATE_GUARD destructor @0x6e53b0 (64-bit build) |

Sent for the demonstration function started by start_demonstrate (demonstration worker loop) and ended by stop_demonstrate. The function detail is named Demonstrate (READ); that the event carries that name is INFERRED. No formatter is installed, so only F members are established. stop_demonstrate ends the function with a final cancel event (no code or error on the wire; internal code 253, not sent), which can arrive before the stop reply (READ; that the skip-end option is unset on this path is INFERRED). A demonstration that ends by itself ends with fail: code 207 when no user location is stored, 501 when a goto fails or times out (READ). The worker only slews the mount (random altitude 5-79 degrees, any azimuth, 120 s goto wait, 5 s dwell) and changes no view. Function-state family (F): the event formatter formats the named function detail. state is always present; stage only when non-empty; lapse_ms while the timer runs or at a terminal state; error and code at fail (even when the stored code is zero; lookup failure gives 'fail to operate'); cancel omits code and error; route is optional function ancestry. The sender does no deduplication and needs no preceding working event. Detail flags can suppress the working or non-working sends while the cached function tree still changes, so a receiver can miss transitions. Channel I (TCP 4700). Delivery: ordinary broadcast to every retained socket of the emitting server (master, guest and never-verified sockets alike); no cadence, delivery or ordering guarantee relative to RPC replies or other events. APK 3.3.2 recognises it and does not require route for it.

Side effects: Observation only for the receiver.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"Demonstrate"`. [INFERRED (event name not read from the emitter)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string with nine fractional digits from a monotonic clock; not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `state` | string | yes | - | F state table; unknown internal codes fall back to idle. One of: `idle`, `working`, `complete`, `fail`, `cancel`. [READ] |
| `stage` | string | if stage string non-empty | - | Only when the detail holds a non-empty stage string; value set unresolved. [READ] |
| `lapse_ms` | integer | if timer started (working) or terminal state | - | Elapsed milliseconds (signed 32-bit low bits): current monotonic time minus start while working or started-but-unfinished, otherwise end minus start. Independent of Timestamp. [READ] |
| `error` | string | if state is fail (F formatter) | - | Message for code. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | if state is fail (F formatter) | - | Stored error code; present at fail even when zero. [READ] |
| `route` | array<string> | no | - | Function-ancestry names at send time (for example View, Stack); may be absent. Not an address. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, working - Started (READ shape; values invented):

```json
{"Event":"Demonstrate","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"working","lapse_ms":0}
```

Event, fail - Failed (READ shape; values invented):

```json
{"Event":"Demonstrate","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"fail","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"lapse_ms":1530}
```
